steps.title: Branch and phase plan
steps.summary: Created branch phase-01-spec from main (Phase 0 merged as f42d833); plan posted and written to status.json. Documentation only: no product code.

steps.title: SPEC §1–3: purpose, terminology, trust model
steps.summary: Goals G1–G8, non-goals, 24-term glossary, parties/trust table, the precise list of what the relay can see, assumptions A-1…A-6 and the fail-closed policy. 1,769 words.

steps.title: SPEC §4: identities and key hierarchy
steps.summary: Identifiers, the SP1 Secret Key (125-bit proposal D-0101 with checksum), Argon2id→HKDF→MUK, OPAQUE auth secret, AK and key bundle, identity keys (Ed25519/X25519/ML-KEM-768), device certification and revocation, VK/IK, rotation table.

steps.title: SPEC §5–6: encryption format and op log
steps.summary: XChaCha20-Poly1305 envelopes, the exact AAD map and record-type enum, the HKDF label table, field rules and failure policy; the signed op DAG, Lamport rules, conflict resolution, signed heads, head pinning with rollback/fork detection, limits.

steps.title: SPEC §7: relay API and transports
steps.summary: OPAQUE register/login, 256-bit tokens stored as SHA-256 with 24 h expiry, all 13 endpoints, head CAS, validation scope, quotas and rate limits, generic error model, storage tables, and the http/folder/memory transports.

steps.title: SPEC §8–11: scoring, sharing, recovery, inventory
steps.summary: Score formula with p/w tables and local-only breach checks; membership ops, HPKE wrapping with bound info, transparency log, safety codes, rotation on removal; recovery kit, 2-of-3 guardians, 72 h window, emergency access; crypto inventory and forward-only versioning.

steps.title: THREAT_MODEL part 1: adversaries A1–A8
steps.summary: Assets table; per-adversary tables for a malicious relay, network, sharee, malicious page, stolen device, malware (explicitly out of scope with reasoning), supply chain and hostile extensions, each with SPEC-linked mitigations and residual risk.

steps.title: THREAT_MODEL part 2: mappings and open risks
steps.summary: The four ETH Zurich 2026 malicious-server classes and the DEF CON 33 DOM clickjacking attack mapped to concrete controls; a 17-row open-risk register (R-0001…R-0112) with severity, status and what closes each; Phase 0 appendix restored.

steps.title: Decisions: PROPOSED entries for every gap
steps.summary: 16 PROPOSED decisions (D-0101…D-0116) covering the Secret Key length, OPAQUE KSF, derived wrapping keys, bundle head pins, X25519-only HPKE, domain separation, enrolment proof, per-object salts, ids, limits, compaction, logout, enumeration, folder layout, the Shamir crate and scoring rules.

steps.title: Diagrams: key hierarchy and trust boundary
steps.summary: Two hand-written SVGs (key hierarchy, relay trust boundary) with dark panels that read on both themes; embedded in SPEC §3.2 and §4.11; XML validated.

steps.title: Preview Docs tab with TOC, tests and screenshots
steps.summary: Safe Markdown parser + DOM renderer (no innerHTML), docs view with contents, Status/Docs tabs with hash routing, ?scroll deep links; 43 tests pass; light/dark desktop and narrow screenshots.

steps.title: Self-attack review, PROGRESS entry and PR
steps.summary: Attacked the design itself: 15 vectors, 10 blocked by named clauses, 5 recorded (R-0106 freeze, R-0113 read-only membership, R-0114 field labels, R-0115 enrolment intent, plus R-0104). Fixes written into SPEC §5.6, §6.9, §9.1; risks filed as issues #32–#34; PROGRESS.md entry; PR closing #7.

risks.title: R-0001 — CodeQL code scanning skipped while the repository is private (issue #23)
R-0002 — Link targets in status.json are trusted from the repository (PR review)
R-0003 — Preview dev server needs style-src 'unsafe-inline' for Vite HMR (loopback only)
R-0004 — gitleaks can miss novel secret formats (manual diff scan)
R-0005 — minimatch advisory in dev-only ESLint tooling
R-0101 — The relay learns metadata: ids, sizes, counts, timing, IP
R-0102 — A device with no pinned head can be rolled back before first verification (TOFU)
R-0103 — A cloned VM or broken RNG could repeat a nonce
R-0104 — Key substitution on first contact before a safety code is verified
R-0105 — A removed member keeps history they already saw; rotation protects future data only
R-0106 — A malicious relay can withhold ops; clients detect but cannot obtain them
R-0107 — Device revocation is time-based; clock skew allows ops just before revoked_at
R-0108 — A weak master password plus a stolen Secret Key allows offline guessing
R-0109 — The printed recovery kit can be photographed or stolen
R-0110 — Key-transparency log is run by the untrusted relay; a split view is possible
R-0111 — The 72-hour recovery window is enforced by the relay
R-0112 — An approved crate or pinned action SHA can still be compromised upstream
R-0113 — v1 membership is write-or-nothing: a 'view only' share cannot be enforced (issue #32, D-0117)
R-0114 — A malicious member can use look-alike field names to phish another member (issue #33)
R-0115 — Device enrolment relies on user intent; show name and fingerprint (issue #34)
